findings.description: The loop condition uses len(self._keys_by_country), which is the number of distinct countries, not the number of cached entries. max_entries is therefore never enforced across postal codes within a country. The cache grows without bound, and with many postal codes per country memory is exhausted. Eviction only happens when there are more countries than max_entries. Eviction then pops the oldest entry, which does not reduce the country count unless that country's last key goes.
findings.title: Eviction bound counts countries, not entries

findings.description: An expired entry is overwritten by _store, and the key set is a set, so duplicates are not an issue. However, expired entries are never purged except by LRU eviction, and the intended size bound is also affected. This is minor compared with the eviction bug.
findings.suggestion: Delete expired entries on lookup, or purge them in _store.
findings.title: Expired entry replaced without removing the old one from the index

findings.description: invalidate_country does `del self._entries[key]` for every key in the index. If the index and entries ever diverge, this raises KeyError. Divergence is possible because the eviction bookkeeping is unreliable. Using pop would be more robust.
findings.title: clear() leaves stale state; invalidate may KeyError

findings.description: source.replace_country is called first, then the cache is invalidated. A concurrent lookup between the two calls can hit a stale cached rate. Worse, a cache miss in that window can load the new rate, which is fine, but stale hits continue until invalidation. The class docstring claims invalidation can never be superseded, yet the source mutation happens outside the cache lock. TableRateSource itself is also not thread-safe.
findings.suggestion: Perform the replacement and invalidation together under the cache lock, or invalidate before and after the replacement.
findings.title: Table replacement and cache invalidation are not atomic
